content: Mayonnaise-based dressings, refrigerated and shelf-stable oil and vinegar-based dressings, creamy dressings, and mayonnaise are included in this category. This also encompasses mayonnaise-type spreads, as well as low-fat and fat-free versions. Examples of sauces in this category include BBQ sauce, Worcestershire sauce, steak sauce, and curry-flavored sauces. Additionally, chili sauces such as Sriracha chili sauce, sweet chili sauce, and mustard are included. Pesto is also part of this category. An interim sodium target of 1005 mg/100g is to be achieved within four years, based on the current median sodium content. This will be followed by further reductions to align with global sodium benchmarks. Soy sauce, fish sauce, and other fermented sauces are included in this category. The interim sodium target is set at 6325 mg/100g, to be achieved within four years, based on the 33rd percentile of current sodium content. Further reductions will follow to meet global benchmarks. Examples of sauces such as teriyaki, black bean, hoisin, stir-fry, duck, and oyster sauces are included. Sweet sauces, chili sauces (e.g., Sriracha and sweet chili), and soy or fish sauces are excluded. The interim sodium target is 2600 mg/100g, to be achieved within four years, based on the current median sodium content, with further reductions planned. Thai and Indian sauces are included in this category. The interim sodium target is 3065 mg/100g, to be achieved within three years, based on the current median sodium content, with further reductions planned to align with global benchmarks. For ready-to-eat savory snacks, such as cheese crackers, soda crackers, and rice cakes, the sodium benchmark is 600 mg/100g. This includes dry breads like Melba toast, rusks, breadsticks, pita chips, and other crisp breads, but excludes unsalted products. Mixed rice crackers with nuts are also included. Approximately 58% of products already meet the global benchmark. For nuts, seeds, and kernels (e.g., popcorn, salted nuts, and seeds), the interim sodium target is 430 mg/100g, to be achieved within four years. While less than one-third of products currently meet the global benchmark, sodium has no technical function in these products beyond flavoring, making the global target of 280 mg/100g achievable. For chips and crisps (e.g., corn, wheat, multigrain, and rice-based), the sodium benchmark is 500 mg/100g. This includes all flavors, such as salt and vinegar, and both reformed and sliced chips. Approximately 33% of products already meet the global benchmark. For extruded snacks (e.g., made from corn, maize, wheat, rice, or potato flour), the sodium benchmark is 520 mg/100g. This includes all flavors and excludes chips and pretzels. Approximately 33% of products already meet the global benchmark. For salted hard pretzels, the sodium benchmark is 760 mg/100g. Approximately 50% of products already meet the global benchmark. For papads and papadums, a separate subcategory is recommended with an interim sodium target of 1390 mg/100g, to be achieved within four years. This will be followed by further reductions toward 600 mg/100g, aligning with similar products like dry breads. For seafoodor meat-based snacks (e.g., fish, squid, or pork-based snacks), a separate category is recommended with an interim sodium target of 1540 mg/100g, to be achieved within four years. These products are commonly consumed in Thailand and other Asian countries and often contain high sodium levels. Further reductions will follow to align with other snack categories. For instant noodles with sauce or seasoning (dry-mix or concentrated), the sodium benchmark is reported as sold rather than as prepared. An interim sodium target of 1730 mg/100g is recommended, to be achieved within four years. This will be followed by further reductions toward the global target of 770 mg/100g. For bread and ordinary bakery products, the sodium benchmark is 310 mg/100g. This includes breads with dried fruit or nuts, refrigerated and frozen dough, and other similar products. Approximately 33% of products already meet the global benchmark. For leavened bread (e.g., yeast-leavened or sourdough bread), the interim sodium target is 445 mg/100g, to be achieved within four years. This includes all types of bread, such as white, whole grain, spelt, rye, and artisanal breads. Further reductions will follow based on compliance reviews.
